## Security Audit: XSS Vulnerability Remediation

**Status**: Open  
**Priority**: CRITICAL  
**Type**: Security Audit  

### Executive Summary

A comprehensive XSS vulnerability scan identified **11 critical/high severity vulnerabilities** across the frontend codebase.

**CRITICAL FINDING**: DOMPurify is NOT INSTALLED - no HTML sanitization is currently in place.

---

## Vulnerability Summary

| Severity | Count | Type |
|----------|-------|------|
| CRITICAL | 8 | Unsanitized HTML Rendering |
| CRITICAL | 3 | ContentEditable XSS |
| HIGH | 1 | URL Injection |

**Total Vulnerabilities**: 11  
**CVSS Score Range**: 7.5 - 9.8

---

## Issue Breakdown

### 1. Infrastructure (Prerequisite)
- **#53** - Install DOMPurify and create sanitization utility
  - **Status**: Must be completed FIRST
  - **Priority**: CRITICAL
  - **Blocks**: All other fixes

### 2. CMS Content Vulnerabilities
- **#54** - Fix XSS in CMS pages (Terms, Privacy, Features)
  - **Files**: 3 pages affected
  - **Severity**: CRITICAL (9.8/10)
  - **Depends on**: #53

### 3. Page Builder Vulnerabilities  
- **#55** - Fix Stored XSS in Visual Page Builder
  - **Files**: VisualPageBuilder.tsx (3 locations)
  - **Severity**: CRITICAL (9.6/10)
  - **Depends on**: #53

### 4. Editor Vulnerabilities
- **#56** - Fix XSS in Rich Text Editor markdown parser
  - **Files**: RichTextEditor.tsx
  - **Severity**: CRITICAL (8.9/10)
  - **Depends on**: #53

### 5. URL Security
- **#57** - Fix URL injection in billing checkout
  - **Files**: billing/page.tsx
  - **Severity**: HIGH (7.5/10)
  - **Depends on**: #53

---

## Implementation Roadmap

### Phase 1: Foundation
- [ ] #53 - Install DOMPurify
- [ ] #53 - Create sanitize.ts utility

### Phase 2: Critical Fixes
- [ ] #54 - Fix CMS pages
- [ ] #55 - Fix Visual Page Builder
- [ ] #56 - Fix Rich Text Editor

### Phase 3: High Priority
- [ ] #57 - Fix billing URL injection
- [ ] Add automated security tests

### Phase 4: Hardening
- [ ] Implement Content Security Policy
- [ ] Add backend input validation
- [ ] Security documentation

---

## Risk Assessment

### Before Remediation
- **Risk Level**: CRITICAL
- **Exploitability**: HIGH
- **Impact**: Site-wide compromise
- **Business Risk**: Data breach, regulatory fines

### After Remediation  
- **Risk Level**: LOW
- **Exploitability**: LOW
- **Impact**: Minimal

---

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 11 vulnerabilities patched
- [ ] DOMPurify installed and configured
- [ ] 100% test coverage for XSS scenarios
- [ ] No new dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization
- [ ] Security code review process established

---

## Issue Dependencies

Start with #53 - all other fixes depend on it:
- #53 (DOMPurify) blocks #54, #55, #56, #57

---

## Timeline

- **Week 1**: Complete #53, #54, #55
- **Week 2**: Complete #56, #57, testing
- **Week 3**: CSP, documentation

**Target Completion**: 3 weeks

---

## References

- OWASP XSS Prevention: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
- DOMPurify: https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify
title: [SECURITY AUDIT] XSS Vulnerability Remediation - Frontend Security Hardening
[SECURITY] Fix URL injection in billing checkout flow

## ðŸš¨ CRITICAL: XSS via Unsafe Markdown Parser **Priority**: CRITICAL **Type**: Security - Reflected/Stored XSS **CWE**: CWE-79 (Cross-Site Scripting) **Severity**: 8.9/10 (CVSS) ### Vulnerability Description The Rich Text Editor implements a custom markdown-to-HTML parser using regex that **does not escape HTML entities**. This allows raw HTML/JavaScript to pass through unchanged and execute in the preview pane. If content is saved, this becomes a **stored XSS vulnerability**. ### Affected File **`frontend/src/components/editor/RichTextEditor.tsx:236-320`** ### Vulnerable Code ```tsx const renderPreview = () => { // â�Œ UNSAFE - Custom parser doesn't escape HTML let html = content .replace(/\*\*(.*?)\*\*/g, '$1') .replace(/\*(.*?)\*/g, '$1') .replace(/`(.*?)`/g, '$1') // ... more regex replacements return { __html: html }; // â�Œ No sanitization }; // Rendered as:
``` ### Attack Scenarios #### Scenario 1: Reflected XSS (Preview Mode) 1. User types in editor: `Hello ` 2. Clicks "Preview" button 3. Custom markdown parser processes content 4. Raw HTML passes through unchanged 5. **Script executes immediately** in preview pane #### Scenario 2: Stored XSS (If Content is Saved) 1. User creates content with embedded script 2. Saves to database 3. Content rendered on public page 4. **All visitors** execute the malicious script ### Why This Happens The custom regex-based markdown parser: - Processes markdown syntax (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) - **BUT** does not escape HTML entities in user input - User input like ` ``` ### Fix Implementation #### Option 1: Sanitize After Markdown Parsing (Quick Fix) ```tsx import { sanitizeHtml } from '@/utils/sanitize'; const renderPreview = () => { let html = content .replace(/\*\*(.*?)\*\*/g, '$1') .replace(/\*(.*?)\*/g, '$1') .replace(/`(.*?)`/g, '$1') // ... other replacements // âœ… CRITICAL FIX: Sanitize after markdown conversion return { __html: sanitizeHtml(html) }; }; ``` #### Option 2: Use Trusted Markdown Library (Recommended) Replace custom parser with a battle-tested library: ```bash npm install marked dompurify npm install --save-dev @types/marked ``` ```tsx import { marked } from 'marked'; import { sanitizeHtml } from '@/utils/sanitize'; const renderPreview = () => { // Parse markdown with trusted library const rawHtml = marked.parse(content); // Sanitize the output return { __html: sanitizeHtml(rawHtml) }; }; ``` **Why use a library?** - Handles edge cases (nested formatting, escaped characters) - Actively maintained and security-audited - Supports full markdown spec - Better performance ### Testing #### Manual Testing 1. Type in editor: `**Bold** and ` 2. Click preview **BEFORE FIX**: Alert executes â�Œ **AFTER FIX**: HTML is escaped, shows as text âœ… #### Automated Testing ```typescript import { sanitizeHtml } from '@/utils/sanitize'; describe('RichTextEditor security', () => { test('escapes HTML in preview', () => { const malicious = '**Bold** '; const preview = renderPreview(malicious); expect(preview.__html).not.toContain('Bold'); }); test('handles image XSS', () => { const malicious = ''; const preview = renderPreview(malicious); expect(preview.__html).not.toContain('onerror'); }); }); ``` ### Comparison: Custom Parser vs Marked | Feature | Custom Regex | Marked + Sanitize | |---------|--------------|-------------------| | **Security** | â�Œ Vulnerable | âœ… Safe | | **HTML Escaping** | â�Œ No | âœ… Yes | | **Full Markdown** | â�Œ Partial | âœ… Complete | | **Maintenance** | â�Œ Manual | âœ… Community | | **Performance** | âœ… Fast | âœ… Fast | ### Dependencies - Requires: #53 (Install DOMPurify) - Optional: Install `marked` for better markdown parsing ### Success Criteria - [ ] Sanitization added to `renderPreview()` - [ ] Manual XSS testing passes - [ ] Automated security tests added - [ ] Consider migrating to `marked` library - [ ] Code review approved ### Migration Path (Optional Enhancement) If migrating to `marked`: 1. Install `marked` and `@types/marked` 2. Replace `renderPreview()` implementation 3. Test markdown rendering matches current behavior 4. Add sanitization with DOMPurify 5. Deploy incrementally ### Impact - **Immediate Risk**: Reflected XSS in editor preview - **Secondary Risk**: If content is saved, becomes stored XSS - **Users Affected**: Editor users (immediate), all users (if saved) ### References - Marked.js: https://marked.js.org/ - XSS via Markdown: https://github.com/commonmark/commonmark-spec/issues/101 - OWASP Markdown XSS: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
title: [SECURITY] Fix XSS in Rich Text Editor custom markdown parser
[SECURITY] Fix Stored XSS in Visual Page Builder (ContentEditable)

# Frontend: Incorrect sync suggestion for enterprise plan

**Labels:** frontend, user-experience

## Error
```
[Pricing] Try manually syncing: POST /api/v1/billing/sync-products
```

## Stack Trace
```
at getPolarProductId (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:83:15)
at PricingPage (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:153:18)
```

## Issue
Same as Issue #4, but occurs when rendering the Ultra (enterprise) plan.

Misleading suggestion - manual sync won't help if CORS blocks the frontend request.

## Fix
See Issue #4 for suggested improvement to conditional error messaging.
title: Frontend: Incorrect sync suggestion for enterprise plan

**Labels:** bug, frontend, polar-integration

Ultra plan should find product with ID `f5ffabdf-e116-4aba-99f3-cdebe0f09486` and `plan_type: "enterprise"`

Same root cause as Issue #1, but for the enterprise plan.

# Frontend: Manual sync suggestion shown incorrectly

**Labels:** frontend, user-experience

## Error
```
[Pricing] Try manually syncing: POST /api/v1/billing/sync-products
```

## Stack Trace
```
at getPolarProductId (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:83:15)
at PricingPage (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:131:18)
```

## Issue
Misleading suggestion - manual sync won't help if CORS blocks the frontend request.

## Suggested Improvement
Only show sync suggestion if API actually returns 200 OK but with empty/wrong data.

Update the error handling logic in `frontend/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` to:
1. Check if the fetch failed due to network/CORS issues
2. Only suggest manual sync if the API returns successfully but with incorrect data
3. Provide different error messages for different failure scenarios
title: Frontend: Manual sync suggestion shown incorrectly

**Labels:** frontend, documentation, user-experience

## Error
```

```

## Stack Trace
```
at getPolarProductId (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:82:15)
at PricingPage (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:131:18)

## Issue
Error message suggests Polar API sync problem, but actual issue is CORS blocking requests.

## Suggested Improvement
Update error message in `frontend/src/app/pricing/page.tsx:82` to:
```typescript
console.error('[Pricing] Failed to load products. Check network tab for CORS or API errors.');
```

This would provide more actionable debugging information to developers.

# Frontend: Empty products array returned from API

**Labels:** bug, frontend, api

## Error
```
[Pricing] Available products: []
```

## Stack Trace
```
at getPolarProductId (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:81:15)
at PricingPage (src\app\pricing\page.tsx:131:18)
```

## Root Cause
CORS preflight rejection causes fetch to fail, returning empty array instead of 3 products.

## Verification
Backend API works correctly:
```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products
# Returns: {"products":[...3 products...]}
```

## Fix
âœ… **FIXED:** Added `http://localhost:8080` to CORS allowed origins in `internal/middleware/cors.go`

Same as Issue #1 - CORS configuration fix resolves this issue.
title: Frontend: Empty products array returned from API
